identity_check: Bruno Fernandes Rocha = ROYAL-BLUE short-sleeve rashguard, black shorts, CYAN tape on the LEFT ankle, tattoo on the left forearm and the right shin. Bryan Silva = navy/black rashguard with a Brazil flag on the right shoulder, black shorts with a white 'GRA...' logo down the leg. Bound to names WITHOUT using the lower-third graphic (whose blue/red blocks are pure left/right design -- the same graphic puts Bruno on the blue side here and on the red side in video 15547218). Instead: the royal-blue/cyan-tape body is the SAME man, kit for kit and tattoo for tattoo, as the athlete in video 15547218 (same event, same day), and Bruno is the only athlete common to both videos, so that body is Bruno. The referee raises HIS arm at t=123 -> Bruno won.
notes: Bout window: engagement begins t~11-16, referee resets them standing t~17-24 (out of bounds at the white line), clock graphic first appears at t=33 reading 5:45 and runs 1:1 with video (5:43@36, 5:39@40, 5:29@50); frozen at 4:28 from t=111 -> finish at t~111, 92s of a 6:00 match. Extrapolating 6:00 from the clock alone gives a start of t=19; the frames show them already fighting at t=12, so ~7s of that is the reset stoppage and bout_start is taken as 11. This graphic shows NO points column at all, so nothing in this bout is scoreboard-corroborated. Camera is far and both kits read dark on a grey mat: top/bottom is only legible from ~t=68 onward, which is why most of the mid-bout reading is dropped rather than corrected. Kept 3 of 9 events read.

log.gemini: Guard Pull / Bryan Silva / transition / true
log.kept_as: Takedown / Bruno Fernandes Rocha / takedown / true @ts 14
log.why: 720p frames t=12/14/16: Bruno charges forward and shoots low (t=14, airborne), and at t=16 he is on top with Bryan under him at the boundary line. Bryan going down is the RESULT of Bruno's attack, not a guard pull he chose. Second look resolves the disagreement in the auditor's favour; ts snapped to the frame that shows the entry.

log.gemini: Guard Pull / Bryan Silva / transition / true
log.why: t=26 is a motion-blurred double engagement and t=29 shows Bruno leaning over a downed Bryan. Consistent with a second takedown by Bruno, but not clearly enough to overturn Gemini's actor -- unresolved disagreement gets no coin flip.

log.gemini: Open Guard / Bryan Silva / guard / true
log.why: t=29-33 the two bodies overlap at the mat edge; which one is underneath is not readable, let alone which guard.

log.gemini: Guard Pass / Bruno Rocha / pass / true
log.why: t=36-48 reads as the DARK-rashguard athlete (Bryan) on top of the blue one, i.e. the opposite of a Bruno pass; but the crop is not clean enough to assert the reverse either. No scoreboard in this broadcast to bound it. Dropped.

log.gemini: Side Control / Bruno Rocha / control / true
log.why: same window as ts 40; the position at t=41-48 is not resolvable and the apparent top man is the wrong one for this claim.

t=56-60 does show Bruno on top, but Bryan is on his side/knees, not mounted. A specific 'Mount' is a claim about a position nobody can see at this distance; the same fact is already carried by the Top Control kept at ts 75.

log.gemini: Turtle Control / Bruno Rocha / control / true
log.kept_as: Top Control / Bruno Fernandes Rocha / control / true @ts 75
log.why: t=70/78/90 at 720p are the clearest frames of the bout: Bruno is unambiguously on top with Bryan FLAT ON HIS BACK. So it is a top control and it is Bruno's, but it is not turtle -- label generalised to the library's generic control per docs/frame_pdf_reading.md 2.5.

log.gemini: Back Control / Bruno Rocha / control / true
log.why: at t=78 and t=90 Bryan is face-up under Bruno, not back-taken. The disagreement is resolved AGAINST the claim, so nothing survives it.

log.kept_as: Submission / Bruno Fernandes Rocha / submission / true @ts 110
log.why: the clock ticks 4:39@100, 4:36@103, 4:34@105, 4:32@107, 4:30@109 and then freezes at 4:28 from t=111 -- so the finish is at t~110-111, not 100, and ts is snapped there. Bruno is on top attacking Bryan's upper body at t=103-111, they separate immediately, and his arm is raised at t=123: a finish with 1:32 unused on a 6:00 clock. That the finish happened, and that it is Bruno's, is visible; WHICH submission is not, so 'Choke' is generalised to 'Submission'.
